madeIn.name: Willendorf II site, Willendorf in der Wachau

object.medium: Carved oolitic limestone with traces of red ochre
object.description: A palm-sized female figure with exaggerated breasts, belly and hips, a patterned head without a face, and no feet. It was carved from an oolitic limestone not found locally and once tinted with red ochre. Found in 1908 in loess deposits beside the Danube at Willendorf, it is the best-known of the Palaeolithic Venus figurines.
facts: Recovered on 7 August 1908 during a dig led by Josef Szombathy, Hugo Obermaier and Josef Bayer.
Radiocarbon dates from the surrounding layers suggest it was buried about 30,000 years ago.
Its limestone is not local to the Wachau; the name Venus is a modern label, and some scholars prefer Woman of Willendorf.
